title: Evaluation of the project “A buddy for seriously ill and their relatives"
summary: People with serious illnesses and their relatives  often face major challenges, such as financial burdens, coping with housework, bureaucratic hurdles with applications and much more. This study evaluates the "Buddy" intervention, which aims to offer low-threshold and proactive support to people with serious illnesses and their relatives. The core element of the programme is trained volunteer and full-time buddies who provide people with serious illnesses and their relatives with support services and accompany them through this difficult phase of their lives. The overall aim of the Buddy project is to achieve optimum care adapted to the individual's way of life and needs as quickly as possible and in a way that minimises the use of resources. The aim of the scientific evaluation is to examine the effects of the Buddy project on people with serious illnesses and their relatives and to identify factors that promote and inhibit its implementation.
conditions: Severe and incurable disease, with an expected lifespan of 12-24 months

interventions.name:
One-armed, social intervention "A buddy in the last year of life"
I.	People with serious illnesses who are supported by a "buddy" 
II. relatives and carers who are (co-) supported by a buddy
III. employed and volunteer buddies

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Participation in the "Buddy" social programme (people with serious illnesses and relatives), employed and volunteer buddies
- Adults capable of giving consent 
- Availability of written consent to participate in the study
- Sufficient knowledge of German
Exclusion criteria:
- Person refuses to participate / is not able to give consent
- No consent / or consent withdrawn later
